name: NeuroPitch™
author: NeuroPitch

sections.description:
NeuroPitch™ helps you increase conversions by displaying contextual offers triggered by user behaviour.

Instead of static popups, NeuroPitch™ reacts to:

  • Time on page
  • Scroll depth
  • Exit intent
  • User intent (cold, warm, hot)
  • Page context

You define your offers. NeuroPitch™ decides when to show them.

The WordPress.org plugin runs fully locally and does not require an external account or external service.

NeuroPitch™ is a product developed and maintained by WEB iDEA.

How it works

  1. Create one or more offers.
  2. Define audience signals such as intent and returning visitors.
  3. Define page context and optional exclusions.
  4. NeuroPitch™ evaluates active offers and selects the best match for the current visitor session.

Minimal setup, zero ongoing maintenance.

Features

  • Behaviour-based triggers: idle pause, scroll depth, and exit intent
  • Weighted scoring engine for offer selection
  • Intent-based targeting: cold / warm / hot
  • Page targeting and exclude pages
  • Returning visitor detection using local browser signals
  • Frequency capping to avoid excessive offer display
  • SPA compatible: re-arms on pushState / popState navigation
  • Debug mode: add ?np_debug=1 to inspect score and matched signals
  • Local statistics: shown events, clicks, and CTR per offer
  • REST API tracking endpoint with nonce verification and rate limiting
  • Caching-plugin compatibility for Autoptimize, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, and W3 Total Cache

Cloud Services (Optional)

NeuroPitch™ may optionally connect to external cloud services hosted at neuropitch.it to provide advanced server-side capabilities such as:

  • Cross-session visitor insights
  • Hosted analytics and aggregated reports
  • Performance breakdowns across campaigns and sites
  • AI-assisted recommendations
  • Experiment reporting and optimisation insights

These services are optional and are not required for the plugin to function.

Documentation: https://neuropitch.it/docs.html

Privacy information: https://neuropitch.it/privacy.html

Privacy

By default, NeuroPitch™ does not send visitor data to external servers.

When the plugin is active, it may store local offer interaction statistics in the site’s own WordPress database, including offer views, clicks, page URL, traffic source, device type, intent level, and score. This data is used to calculate local offer statistics.

The plugin also uses browser storage such as sessionStorage and localStorage for frequency capping, in-session behaviour, and basic return-visit signals.

The WordPress.org plugin does not create user accounts, does not require an external account, and does not transmit personal data to neuropitch.it by default.

Site owners are responsible for disclosing behavioural features and local analytics in their own privacy policy where required.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the neuropitch folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it through the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to NeuroPitch™ in the admin menu.
  4. Create your first offer and activate the plugin.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require an external service?

No. The WordPress.org plugin works fully locally and does not require an external account.

What are cloud services?

Optional external services that may extend the plugin with hosted analytics, cross-session insights, and server-side recommendations.

Does it work with page builders like Elementor?

Yes. NeuroPitch™ loads as standalone frontend scripts and does not depend on any page builder.

Is it compatible with caching plugins?

Yes. NeuroPitch™ registers exclusions for common optimisation plugins including Autoptimize, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, and W3 Total Cache.

Does it slow down my site?

No. The frontend scripts are lightweight and run locally in the browser.

What data does the plugin store?

The plugin uses browser storage such as sessionStorage and localStorage to manage in-session behaviour, frequency capping, and basic return-visit signals. Event statistics such as shown events and clicks are stored in the site’s own WordPress database.

Is it GDPR compliant?

NeuroPitch™ is designed to avoid collecting personal data by default. Website owners remain responsible for informing their visitors about any behavioural features used on their site and for complying with applicable privacy laws.

How do I test it without waiting for triggers?

Add ?np_debug=1 to any page URL. Debug mode shows the score and matched signals directly in the widget.
